claim_b.current_score: low (pre-DR); upgraded to high in stages-validated/stage-2-pain-points.md post-DR
claim_b.source_url: https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2013/09/06/high-logistics-costs-impede-higher-economic-growth-for-indonesia (World Bank 2013 press release, post-DR primary citation)

contradictions.delta_description: Stage 1 uses 23% (Bappenas 2022/2023 current figure: 14.29% domestic + 8.98% export = 23.27%); Stage 2 uses 24% (World Bank 2013 historical figure: 24.64% for 2011 data). Both are now supported by primary-multilateral and primary-gov sources after DR. They represent the same structural phenomenon at different measurement years — 2011 (WB 2013) vs 2022/2023 (Bappenas). The DR on pp-2.3-2 explicitly resolved this: 'Stage 1 and Stage 2 figures (23% vs. 24%) should be reconciled in the final artifact as reflecting different measurement years of the same underlying structural problem.' The validated drafts now cite both figures in parallel (Stage 1 notes historical 24% context; Stage 2 notes current 23.27%). However, the Stage 2 validated narrative headline still leads with '24% of GDP' while Stage 1 leads with '23%' — a reader comparing sections may perceive a contradiction that is actually a temporal split.
contradictions.resolution_suggestion: Both stages should use a unified formulation: 'Indonesia total logistics costs represent approximately 23–24% of GDP — 24% per the World Bank 2013 report (2011 data) and 23.27% per Bappenas/BPS 2022/2023 data — versus Malaysia at 13% and Thailand at 15–20%.' Stage 2's validated header already moves toward this; confirm the same reconciliation note is visible in Stage 1 body text to avoid reader confusion. No revision needed if the drafts are read in isolation — this is a presentation-layer harmonization note, not a factual error.

claim_a.value: 15.7% (2023 baseline) sourced to Berg Insight primary research

claim_b.value: 15.7% (2023 baseline) still attributed to ResearchAndMarkets via GlobeNewswire (aggregator, Tier 6)
claim_b.current_score: low (aggregator auto-downgrade, stages-validated/stage-4-pain-points.md footnote 9 still cites GlobeNewswire)

contradictions.delta_description: Deep research on Stage 3 (pp3-4 DR) established that the 15.7% and 25.7% figures originate from Berg Insight primary research (specialist Tier 3 telematics analyst), not from a Tier 6 aggregator. The GlobeNewswire URL is merely the press-release channel Berg Insight used to distribute its own report — the underlying research is non-aggregator. Stage 3's validated markdown reflects this upgrade (footnotes 58 and 59 cite Berg Insight 1st and 2nd Ed directly). Stage 4's validated markdown still carries the pre-DR attribution (footnote 9 cites 'ResearchAndMarkets, Southeast Asia Fleet Management Market Report 2024' via GlobeNewswire) and the confidence score for this claim remains Low. The same figures appear in both stages with different attributed sources and different confidence tiers — a Class C DR-not-applied contradiction. This matters because Stage 4 uses the 15.7% figure as a load-bearing anchor for three pain points (PP4.1, PP4.3, PP4.5) related to SEA supply-chain visibility, and the aggregator attribution actively suppresses its credibility.
contradictions.resolution_suggestion: Apply the Berg Insight citation upgrade to Stage 4's footnote 9 (and any other occurrences of the ResearchAndMarkets/GlobeNewswire citation for this metric). Replace with: 'Berg Insight, Fleet Management in Southeast Asia, 1st Edition (Oct 2024; Tier 3 specialist analyst): 2.8M installed base; 15.7% penetration (2023) → 25.7% by 2028; CAGR 13.7% — updated in 2nd Edition (Feb 2026) to 17.5% (2024) → 27.1% (2029). Public brochure: https://media.berginsight.com/2024/10/25195648/bi-fmsoutheastasia1-ps.pdf.' Confidence score upgrades from Low to Medium per the Stage 3 DR rationale.

contradictions.resolution_suggestion: Annotate claim pp-1.1-8 in pass-2-validation/stage-1.json with a DR outcome note: 'REFINED by DR (pp-1.1-8 DR): The FMCSA April 2025 identity verification launch is confirmed by Tier 1 FMCSA sources. HOWEVER, the pass-2-validation/stage-6.json still carries the old $2.8B+ (VC36) and $4B (PP6.5-cost3) claim texts without DR-outcome annotation — so the validation JSON contradicts the corrected canonical artifacts.
contradictions.resolution_suggestion: The canonical stage-6 artifacts are already corrected (both harmonized to ~$3.4B with Delaware bankruptcy court citation). The pass-2-validation/stage-6.json needs annotation on VC36 and PP6.5-cost3 noting: 'DR RESOLVED: both figures superseded by court-verified $3.36B (~$3.4B) per Vesttoo investigation report, US Bankruptcy Court District of Delaware Case 23-11160. Canonical artifacts updated. The $2.8B+ was the CCB-specific sub-portion; the $4B was a pre-investigation media estimate.' No curator action needed on the canonical artifacts — this is a pass-2 JSON annotation gap only.

[NEEDS-ATTENDED-FETCH: https://www.gartner.com/en/documents/3989061].' Score should remain Low until the Gartner document is fetched. The FedEx Future of Logistics 2025 survey (n=700, stage-4 footnote 7) provides independent corroboration of the general multi-system coordination burden and should be highlighted as the stronger open-source anchor for this pain point.

narrative: Three high-severity contradictions were found, all of Class C (DR verdict not fully propagated): Stage 4 still carries the discredited ResearchAndMarkets attribution for the SEA telematics 15.7% figure despite the Stage 3 DR upgrading it to Berg Insight primary research; Stage 6's pass-2 validation JSON retains the superseded $2.8B/$4B Vesttoo figures that the DR resolved to ~$3.4B (court-verified); and Stage 6's validation JSON still registers the three MarketGrowthReports WH5 percentages (12%/25%/23%) that the DR established as confirmed-scarce and the canonical artifact has already dropped. In all three cases the canonical stage-N artifacts (stages-validated/) are already corrected — the gap is that the pass-2-validation JSONs lack DR-outcome annotations, creating a validation record that contradicts the canonical artifacts. No cross-stage factual contradictions requiring curator judgment on which value is correct were found; the Indonesia GDP logistics cost (23% vs 24%) is a temporal measurement split, not a factual dispute, and is already reconciled in both canonical artifacts.
